title: Templates gallery
description: "Browse the blueprint catalogue and deploy a template from the dashboard."
---

import { Step, Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

**Purpose** — The gallery is the catalogue of ready-made blueprints. You browse it on the web at [templates.notploy.com](https://templates.notploy.com) or directly from a project environment, and Notploy turns the selected blueprint into a deployable Compose service.

## Where blueprints come from

| Source | When it is used |
| --- | --- |
| **Public gallery** (`https://templates.notploy.com`) | Default for every Notploy installation. |
| **Local checkout** | You run Notploy from the repository: blueprints are read from `templates/blueprints`, so a blueprint you just added is usable without publishing anything. |
| **Custom base URL** | You host your own gallery. Set the **Base URL (optional)** field of the template dialog; your browser remembers it. |

<Callout type="info">
The panel asks the chosen source for its catalogue (`/meta.json`) and downloads `docker-compose.yml`,
`template.toml` and `instructions.md` only for the blueprint you select.
</Callout>

## Deploy a blueprint

<Steps>
<Step>
**Open the template dialog.** In a project environment, click **Create Service → Template**.
The dialog is titled *Create from Template*.
</Step>
<Step>
**Find the blueprint.** Use the search box, filter by tags, or show only your bookmarks (star icon).
The view toggle switches between a detailed card layout and a compact icon grid. Each card links to
the project's GitHub repository, website and documentation.
</Step>
<Step>
**Create the service.** Click **Create** and confirm. When several targets are possible, pick a
**Server** — this step is mandatory on Notploy Cloud and when the instance is configured to deploy
to remote servers only.
</Step>
<Step>
**Deploy.** Notploy creates a Compose service named after the blueprint, resolves every variable,
writes the environment, creates the mounts and domains declared by the template, and attaches the
blueprint logo. Open the service and click **Deploy**.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="warn" title="Secrets are generated once">
Helpers such as `${password}`, `${hash}` or `${jwt}` run when the service is created, not on every
deployment. Review the generated values in the **Environment** tab before the first deploy, and
change them there whenever you need to.
</Callout>

After deployment the blueprint behaves like any other [Compose stack](/docs/core/docker-compose):
edit the file, add [domains](/docs/core/docker-compose/domains), mount [utilities](/docs/core/docker-compose/utilities) and roll out updates from the service page.

## Browse the public gallery

The web gallery is a static site that mirrors the same catalogue:

- **Search and filter** — the query lives in the URL (`?q=`), tags combine with AND semantics, and the grid/rows toggle switches layout.
- **Template dialog** — opens with the *Instructions* tab when the blueprint ships a guide, plus *Docker Compose* and *Configuration* tabs with copy buttons.
- **Base64 Configuration** — an encoded bundle of the compose file and the configuration, ready to paste into Notploy (see below).
- **Edit Template** — links straight to the blueprint folder in the Notploy repository, and **Add Template** opens a GitHub issue for missing blueprints.

→ Browse the gallery at [templates.notploy.com](https://templates.notploy.com)

## Import a Base64 configuration

Any source that can produce a Base64 bundle can create or reconfigure a Compose service:

1. **Create Service → Import** — give the service a name and an app name, paste the payload and confirm the preview.
2. On an existing Compose service, open the **Advanced** tab and use **Import** to replace that service's configuration.

The payload is the Base64 encoding of a JSON object with two plain-text fields:

```json
{
  "compose": "services:\n  grafana:\n    image: grafana/grafana:latest\n",
  "config": "[[config.domains]]\nserviceName = \"grafana\"\nport = 3000\n"
}
```

Generate it from the two files of any blueprint:

```bash
jq -n --rawfile compose docker-compose.yml --rawfile config template.toml \
  '{compose: $compose, config: $config}' | base64 | tr -d '\n'
```

<Callout type="warn" title="Import replaces the service configuration">
Importing a payload overwrites the compose file and environment, and recreates the mounts and
domains of the target service. Keep a copy of anything you want to restore.
</Callout>
